Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: No evidence found of a functioning government services portal linked to digital ID authentication in Guinea. Simandou 2040 digital strategy references digital services but no confirmed government portal using digital ID for authentication.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light check surfaced two live government portals — Service Public Guinée (service-public.gov.gn), which lists ID-related services (biometric ID card, passport, driving licence, civil status documents), and the E-GOV applications portal (app.gov.gn), which supports account creation and login with 'existing government credentials'. Neither page explicitly confirms that authentication on these portals is performed via the national digital ID credential (e.g. biometric verification or ID-linked single sign-on) rather than a standard username/password account. Evidence is suggestive of a centralised portal existing but inconclusive on digital-ID-based authentication specifically, so the score is not changed on this basis alone. Flagged for human review to determine whether these portals meet the digital-ID-authentication threshold.
revised_comments: Guinea operates a centralised government services portal (service-public.gov.gn) and an E-GOV applications portal (app.gov.gn) offering online access to civil registration, biometric ID card, passport and driving licence services, with account-based login using government credentials. Whether authentication on these platforms draws specifically on the national digital identity credential is not confirmed in publicly available documentation.

revised_comments: No individual self-service mechanism through which citizens can view the data held about them in the identity database, or see how it has been accessed, has been identified. Guinea's data protection law (Law No. L/2016/037/AN) grants data subjects rights of access, rectification and erasure in principle, but no operational portal or documented procedure for exercising this right in relation to the ID system is publicly available.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: Law No. L/2016/037/AN provides for the creation of a national data protection authority (CNIL), but as of available sources the authority has not yet been established. Data Protection Africa notes 'has not yet been established'. No effective DPA oversight in practice.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown had no cited source. Verification finds clear, consistent evidence across two independent legal-tracking sources (DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World, last reviewed 2021; Africa Data Protection portal, undated) that although Law No. L/2016/037/AN of 2016 provides for a national data protection authority (CNIL) to be created by regulation, this authority has still not been established. This is a definite 'No' rather than an 'Unknown', so the value code is revised from 0 to 1. No news reporting found through mid-2026 indicates the CNIL has since been created; a 2025 presidential decree on data security addresses civil-registration authentication only and does not establish a general DPA.
revised_comments: Law No. L/2016/037/AN of 2016 on cybersecurity and personal data protection provides for a national data protection authority (Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés, CNIL) to be created by regulation, but this authority has not been established. There is consequently no dedicated body providing oversight of ID-related data collection and sharing in Guinea.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: No evidence found of Guinea's digital ID being linked to SIM card registration requirements. SIM card registration may exist using traditional ID, but no confirmed digital ID/MOSIP linkage to SIM registration found.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown had no cited source. Verification finds that Guinea's telecoms regulator ARPT has required identification (national ID card, passport or voter card) for SIM registration since Decision D/001/ARPT/CNRPT/2021 (in force since 31 December 2020, implementing Article 36 of Law L/2015/018/AN). A new presidential decree (D/2026/0161/PRG/SGG, dated 22 June 2026) goes further, deploying a national identity-certification platform for SIM cardholders; press reporting (Guinée114, 22 May 2026) confirms no SIM can be activated, reactivated or replaced without prior identity validation via this platform. This makes identity verification effectively mandatory for SIM registration, so the value code is revised from 0 to 3 (Mandatory).
revised_comments: Identity verification is mandatory for SIM card activation, reactivation and replacement in Guinea. Subscribers must present a national identity card, passport or voter card (Decision D/001/ARPT/CNRPT/2021, implementing Article 36 of the 2015 Telecommunications Law), and a 2026 presidential decree has deployed a national platform through which the regulator ARPT certifies the identity of SIM cardholders before any SIM can be activated, reactivated or replaced.
